posts.why: The mismatch is visible in one screenshot.

tiktok.hook: This business answers four questions nobody asked. None of the four.
tiktok.vo: This page answers four questions nobody asked: our journey, our values, our vision, and our commitment to excellence. It does not answer the four that matter: how much, where are you, when can I get it, and how do I pay. The questions nobody asked are the ones the owner wanted to answer. The ones that matter are the ones the customer walked in with.
tiktok.cap: Answers: journey, values, vision. Questions: price, location, timing, payment.
tiktok.body: The page answers journey, values, vision and commitment. It does not answer how much, where, when, or how to pay. The owner answered what they wanted to talk about, not what the customer walked in with.

instagram.cap:
Price, place, timing, payment. They are unglamorous, they are the whole decision, and they are almost always the last thing a business writes about itself.

The missing four are always the boring four.

facebook.body:
A page I read answers four questions nobody asked: our journey, our values, our vision, our commitment to excellence.

It does not answer the four that matter: how much, where are you, when can I get it, how do I pay.

The questions nobody asked are the ones the owner wanted to answer. The ones that matter are the ones the customer arrived with.

Which four are missing from yours?

posts.why: Letting a buyer's sentence carry the post is the most credible format.

tiktok.hook: Someone bought the chat pack and sent one line. Here it is.
tiktok.vo: Someone bought the chat pack and sent one line afterwards. It said: I used the price one and the man paid without arguing, first time in two years. I am not going to add anything to that, because anything I add would be me talking over the only useful review I have.
tiktok.cap: "I used the price one and the man paid without arguing, first time in two years."
tiktok.body: One line from a real buyer, unedited: the price script, and the customer paid without arguing for the first time in two years. Anything added to that would be talking over the only review that matters.

instagram.cap:
The most useful thing you can publish is a customer's own sentence, unedited, with permission. It does not need a design.

One sentence, forwarded, is worth a page of adjectives.

facebook.body:
Someone bought the chat pack and sent one line afterwards:

'I used the price one and the man paid without arguing, first time in two years.'

I am not adding anything to that, because anything I add would be me talking over the only useful review I have.

If you have one of these, post it. Unedited.

posts.why: Knowing the entry point changes how you write the pack.

tiktok.hook: Almost every buyer opens the checklist first. Not the guide. The checklist.
tiktok.vo: Almost every buyer opens the checklist first, not the twenty page guide, because a list can be finished and a guide can only be started. Which means if you sell anything with a guide and a checklist, the checklist is the product and the guide is the reference. Put the list first in the folder, name it clearly, and watch how differently people use it.
tiktok.cap: The checklist is the product. The guide is the reference. Order the folder that way.
tiktok.body: A list can be finished; a guide can only be started. So the checklist is the product and the guide is the reference, which means the checklist goes first in the folder.

instagram.cap:
This applies to onboarding, welcome emails, and any document with more than three pages. People complete short things and bookmark long ones.

Design for what gets finished, not what gets admired.

facebook.body:
Almost every buyer opens the checklist first. Not the twenty-page guide. The checklist.

Because a list can be finished and a guide can only be started.

So if you sell anything with both, the checklist is the product and the guide is the reference. Put the list first in the folder and name it plainly.

What is first in yours?

posts.why: A product principle stated as a rule.

tiktok.hook: A template is only useful if it is editable. Otherwise, a poster.
tiktok.vo: A template is only useful if it is editable, in software you already have, without a subscription. A locked PDF is a poster, and posters decorate a room without changing anything in it. Which is why everything we sell opens in Word, Excel or a plain text file, and why I will keep saying that until the rest of the market stops shipping locked files.
tiktok.cap: Editable, in software you already own. A locked PDF is a poster.
tiktok.body: It has to be editable in software you already have, without a subscription. A locked PDF is a poster: it decorates a room without changing anything in it.

instagram.cap:
This is the first question to ask about any template, and almost nobody asks it until they discover the file will not open.

Ask what software it opens in before you buy it.

facebook.body:
A template is only useful if it is editable — in software you already have, without a subscription.

A locked PDF is a poster. It decorates a room without changing anything in it.

Everything we sell opens in Word, Excel or a plain text file, and I will keep saying that until the market stops shipping locked files.

What was the last locked file you bought?

posts.topic: The buyer who rewrote it in Pidgin
posts.why: Celebrating an edit is what makes the product real.

tiktok.hook: A buyer rewrote our script in Pidgin and sent it back.
tiktok.vo: A buyer rewrote one of our scripts entirely in Pidgin and sent it to me as a thank you. Same structure, same three sentences, entirely his voice, and it was better than mine for his customer. That is not a problem with the script, that is the script working. A template you cannot personalise is a script you will never send.
tiktok.cap: He rewrote it in Pidgin. That is the template working, not failing.
tiktok.body: Same structure, three sentences, entirely his voice — and better than mine for his customer. A template you cannot personalise into your own words is a script you will never send.

instagram.cap:
This is why we send editable files. The value is the shape of the sentence, not the vocabulary inside it.

The words should sound like you. The structure can be borrowed.

facebook.body:
A buyer rewrote one of our scripts entirely in Pidgin and sent it to me as a thank you.

Same structure. Same three sentences. Entirely his voice — and better than mine for his customer.

That is not a problem with the script. That is the script working.

A template you cannot personalise is a script you will never send.

Have you ever rewritten someone's template?

posts.topic: Edit every script into your voice
posts.why: The instruction that turns a purchase into a result.

tiktok.hook: A script in the wrong voice is worse than no script.
beats: Change the words you would not say
tiktok.vo: Edit every script into your own voice before you send it. Read it out loud, change every word you would not say at the counter, and cut one sentence entirely. A script in somebody else's voice is worse than no script, because the customer can hear the costume, and a costume in a negotiation reads as a business that does not know what it is doing.
tiktok.cap: Read it out loud. Change what you would not say. Cut one line. Now it is yours.
tiktok.body: Read it out loud, change every word you would not say at the counter, cut one sentence. A script in someone else's voice is worse than none, because the customer can hear the costume.

instagram.cap:
This is a five minute edit, and it is the difference between sounding like a professional and sounding like a leaflet.

The costume is always audible in a negotiation.

facebook.body:
Edit every script into your own voice before you send it.

Read it out loud. Change every word you would not say at the counter. Cut one sentence entirely.

A script in somebody else's voice is worse than no script, because the customer can hear the costume — and a costume in a negotiation reads as a business that does not know what it is doing.

Which word would you change first?

posts.topic: Nobody's first attempt sounds like them
posts.why: Normalises the rewrite, which is where most people quit.

tiktok.hook: Nobody's first attempt sounds like them. Rewrite it twice.
tiktok.vo: Nobody's first attempt sounds like them, and that includes professional writers. The first draft is stiff because you are trying to be correct. The second is clearer because you stopped performing. The third sounds like you, because by then you are bored of yourself and boredom is where the voice lives. So do three, and send the third.
tiktok.cap: First draft: correct. Second: clear. Third: yours. Send the third.
tiktok.body: The first draft is stiff because you are trying to be correct. The second is clearer because you stopped performing. By the third you are bored of yourself, and boredom is where the voice lives.

instagram.cap:
This is a useful thing to know before you decide you are bad at writing. You are not bad at it, you are on draft one.

Boredom is where your voice lives.

facebook.body:
Nobody's first attempt sounds like them — including professional writers.

Draft one is stiff, because you are trying to be correct. Draft two is clearer, because you stopped performing. Draft three sounds like you, because by then you are bored of yourself — and boredom is where the voice lives.

Do three. Send the third.

Which draft are you sending?

posts.topic: Would you use someone else's words
posts.why: The condition is the product spec.

tiktok.hook: I asked if people would use words someone else wrote for them.
beats: Only if I can change them
Which is why ours are editable
tiktok.vo: I asked people whether they would use words somebody else wrote for them. Most said yes, with one condition: only if I can change them. Which is the entire product specification, arrived at by strangers in four seconds. Not better words. Editable words. Words you can bend into the way you actually talk, because the customer has met you and will notice if the message sounds like a company.
tiktok.cap: "Only if I can change them." That is the whole product spec.
tiktok.body: Most said yes, with one condition: only if I can change them. Not better words — editable words, bent into the way you actually talk, because your customer has met you.

instagram.cap:
This is the answer that shaped what we ship: Word and Excel, never locked, never behind a subscription.

Editable is the feature. Everything else is packaging.

facebook.body:
I asked people whether they would use words somebody else wrote for them.

Most said yes, with one condition: 'Only if I can change them.'

That is the entire product specification, arrived at by strangers in four seconds. Not better words. Editable words — bent into the way you actually talk, because the customer has met you.

Would you use a script you could not edit?

posts.why: The refusal defines ownership in one line.

tiktok.hook: Someone asked us to lock the files. We said no.
tiktok.vo: Someone suggested we lock the files so buyers could not change them, to protect the brand voice. We said no, twice. Locking a file protects the writer's ego, not the buyer's business, and the words stop being useful the moment they cannot be bent into the way a real person talks. You buy the words. They are yours. Cross them out.
tiktok.cap: You bought the words. They are yours. Cross them out.
tiktok.body: Locking protects the writer's ego, not the buyer's business. The words stop being useful the moment they cannot be bent into the way a real person talks.

instagram.cap:
Ownership is the difference between a purchase and a rental, and buyers can feel which one they are getting.

A locked template is a museum piece. You need a tool.

facebook.body:
Someone suggested we lock the files so buyers could not change them, to protect the brand voice.

We said no, twice.

Locking a file protects the writer's ego, not the buyer's business. The words stop being useful the moment they cannot be bent into the way a real person talks.

You buy the words. They are yours. Cross them out.

What have you been sold that you could not edit?

posts.why: One action, with a deadline and a use date.

tiktok.hook: Tonight, rewrite one script in your own words. Then use it tomorrow.
tiktok.vo: Tonight, pick one script, rewrite it in your own words, read it out loud once, and send it to a real customer tomorrow. Not all thirty six. One. Rewritten, said out loud, sent within twenty four hours. That is the whole homework, and the people who do it are the only ones who ever tell me the pack worked.
tiktok.cap: One script. Rewritten tonight. Sent tomorrow. That is the whole homework.
tiktok.body: Not all thirty-six. One, rewritten, said out loud once, sent within twenty-four hours. The people who do that are the only ones who ever report back.

instagram.cap:
Twenty-four hours is the difference between a purchase and a folder. Put the deadline on yourself before the enthusiasm fades.

A pack becomes useful the moment one line leaves your phone.

facebook.body:
Tonight: pick one script, rewrite it in your own words, read it out loud once, and send it to a real customer tomorrow.

Not all thirty-six. One.

Rewritten, said out loud, sent within 24 hours.

Will you do it?
